mission.title: At the Doctor's: Symptoms and Advice

theory.title: Describing symptoms and talking to a doctor
theory.explanation: Use have got to describe many symptoms: I've got a headache. You can also use have + a + symptom: I have a cold. Use hurt to say that a part of your body is painful: My back hurts. Ask What's the matter? or How do you feel? to find out about someone's health. Use feel + adjective: I feel dizzy. Use should/shouldn't to give simple health advice.
theory.tip: Use has got with he/she/it: She's got a sore throat. With hurt, add -s after he/she/it: His tooth hurts.

patterns.label: Block 5 · Have got questions
examples: Have you got a sore throat?

patterns.label: Block 10 · Shouldn't for advice
examples: You shouldn't go to work today.
You shouldn't do sport with a fever.

items.prompt: You shouldn't ___ to work with a fever.

content.passage: Emma doesn't feel well today. She has got a headache and a sore throat, and she feels very tired. Her mother phones the local clinic and makes an appointment for ten thirty. At the clinic, the doctor asks, 'What's the matter?' Emma says that her throat hurts when she speaks. The doctor checks her temperature, but she hasn't got a fever. The doctor says she should drink plenty of water and get some rest. She shouldn't go swimming or play tennis for a few days. The doctor gives her some medicine for her sore throat. Emma feels better after a quiet afternoon at home.

content.audioTranscript: Good morning, Green Road Clinic. How can I help? Hello, I'd like to make an appointment. I have had a Tuesday since yesterday, and now I've got a headache. Does your throat hurt too? Yes, a little. Have you got a temperature? No, I don't think so. We have an appointment at ten fifteen this morning. That's perfect. Please bring your health card and arrive five minutes early. The doctor may tell you to get some rest and drink plenty of water. If you need any medicine, there's a pharmacy opposite the clinic. Remember to take it twice a day, if the doctor recommends it.
